blocks.text: How the research grid works: rows, columns, tiers and prices.
Research costs spice (Mods cost some minerals too). One project at a time; a paused one keeps its progress.
The cost is paid gradually while the project runs, not up front. If you run out of spice, progress stalls until you have more.

In single player the match waits while the research screen is open. It opens by itself at the start of a match (on the Logistics tab) and whenever a project finishes with nothing else running (on that tech's tab), so research never sits idle unnoticed.
Each tab is a grid: one row per line of upgrades, and columns Basic, Advanced and Experimental. Each cell is a stack of tiers, researched top-down.
Each tier below needs only the one above it in its stack; nothing is locked by column.
In tech descriptions, a + or - means the tech adds that much on top of the tier before; "now" gives the new total once it's researched.
The columns trade cost against power. Basic techs give the most value for the price and often pay for themselves (the Harvest line).
Experimental techs give the least value for the price, but the most powerful effects. Advanced sits in between.
Mods follow their own rules: see the Mods page.
Bonuses of the same kind add; different kinds multiply.
Each tab's page here shows its tree with a note under every tech: exact numbers, what it touches, how it stacks, and when it is worth the time.
